decisions.chosen_approach: Change both the Python and C open() guards so binary mode accepted encoding="locale"

evidence.quote: On 2021-03-31, `ff3c9739...` changed both the Python and C `open()` guards so binary mode accepted `encoding="locale"`. Its commit message framed the change as making the value usable everywhere that `encoding=None` was allowed.

decisions.rationale: Making the value usable everywhere that encoding=None was allowed
decisions.subject: Allow binary mode in open() guards to accept encoding="locale"

decisions.chosen_approach: Explicitly revert commit ff3c9739... and restore the unconditional rule that binary mode rejects every non-None encoding
constraints: binary mode rejects every non-None encoding

evidence.quote: Later the same day, `cfa17668...` explicitly reverted that commit and restored the unconditional rule that binary mode rejects every non-`None` encoding. The final PEP remained in force; only the over-broad implementation was reverted.

decisions.rationale: The final PEP remained in force; only the over-broad implementation was reverted.
decisions.subject: Restore unconditional rejection of non-None encodings in binary mode

decisions.chosen_approach: Make "locale" a valid encoding value for io.TextIOWrapper rather than a codec alias
constraints: This is a text-encoding feature. It does not establish an encoding parameter for binary streams.

evidence.quote: The specification makes `"locale"` a valid `encoding` value for `io.TextIOWrapper`.
The rationale says `"locale"` is not a codec alias because the locale may change at runtime and because `TextIOWrapper` has device-encoding behavior.
This is a text-encoding feature. It does not establish an encoding parameter for binary streams.
